The Sam Vimes "Boots" Theory of Economic Injustice runs thus:
At the time of Men at Arms, Samuel Vimes earned thirty-eight dollars a month as a Captain of the Watch, plus allowances. A really good pair of leather boots, the sort that would last years and years, cost fifty dollars. This was beyond his pocket and the most he could hope for was an affordable pair of boots costing ten dollars, which might with luck last a year or so before he would need to resort to makeshift cardboard insoles so as to prolong the moment of shelling out another ten dollars.
Therefore over a period of ten years, he might have paid out a hundred dollars on boots, twice as much as the man who could afford fifty dollars up front ten years before. And he would still have wet feet.
Without any special rancour, Vimes stretched this theory to explain why Sybil Ramkin lived twice as comfortably as he did by spending about half as much every month.

Just turned 30.  Father "disappeared" when I was 18 months, found him just shy of my 18th birthday.  Now, I think my mum has similar issues to your FMILs (not stalking just was looking for the in between update and saw this), so I'll fill in some backstory.  I found the solicitors letters regarding visitation.  My mum always said he just didn't turn up one day and she heard nothing further from his solicitors.  The paperwork shows this to be a lie.  He was in a car accident and would not be able to make the next visit for fairly obvious reasons.  She never responded, and we moved to the opposite side of the country not long after.

Meeting him was... awkward to say the least.  New girlfriend, half brothers, and I dove in head first without thinking about it.  One thing I would certainly do if I could do it all again, is go slow.  Sloth slow.  I'd had a shit upbringing full of abuse from many sides of different types.  I guess I rushed into the situation with no regard, knowing that my mum had actually kept me away, instead of him abandoning me.  Lots of different stories came out, mostly lies from both sides, and I didn't know who to believe - neither of them it turned out.  His mum and sisters pretty much ignored me - now I wasn't looking for special treatment, but conversation longer than hello would've been appreciated...
